subject.title: [Feature]: Update CODEOWNERS to reflect documented maintainer area ownership

question: Should OpenClaw convert the documented maintainer area list into enforced CODEOWNERS review routing for gateway, agents, CLI, cron, and commands?
rationale: The code change is small, but the durable effect is reviewer governance and repository access policy; automation cannot safely choose who should be auto-requested or whether broad enforced ownership is desired.

options.title: Confirm a narrow owner-approved mapping
options.body: Ask the project lead and listed area owners to approve specific CODEOWNERS entries, then land only those confirmed routes while preserving secops precedence.

options.title: Keep centralized routing
options.body: Decline broad area CODEOWNERS for now and close this issue with the rationale that manual triage avoids enforced review noise.

options.title: Use teams instead of individuals
options.body: Create or reuse GitHub teams for review routing so CODEOWNERS can avoid long individual lists, if repository administration supports that model.

recommendation.title: Confirm a narrow owner-approved mapping
recommendation.body: Ask the project lead and listed area owners to approve specific CODEOWNERS entries, then land only those confirmed routes while preserving secops precedence.

likelyOwner.reason: The current CODEOWNERS file routes ownership-rule changes to this handle, and `CONTRIBUTING.md` names Peter Steinberger as project lead.
